title: A2-01 · Root and scheme: how Arab morphology works

blocks.text: A2-01 · Root and scheme: how Arab morphology works
Lesson overview

In A1, you saw that ⁧كِتَاب⁩ , ⁧مَكْتَب⁩ , ⁧مَكْتَبَة⁩ and ⁧يَكْتُبُ⁩ share the same three consonants. In this unit, that observation becomes a practical tool: the root ( ⁧الجِذْر⁩ ) carries a general idea, while the pattern ( ⁧الوَزْن⁩ ) turns it into a verb, a person, a place or an action. With around twenty common patterns, you can understand words you have never studied and find them in a dictionary. For anyone reading Arabic sources, this is the most useful skill at this level. Two weeks.

rows: A2 · Module A2.1 The verbal system
Examination A1 exceeded (at least 70%, each section at least 60%)
12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 49–50 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-01), voice synthesis script, a root-ordered dictionary (Appendix C), session with the tutor in the second week
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. identify the root of a regular word by removing article, prefixes, long vowels and endings;

2. recognize the most frequent patterns and their value: fāʿil "Those who do" are: mafʿūl "what it suffers" mafʿal / mafʿala Place (s) of origin fiʿāla and faʿl The action shall be: mifʿāl The following definitions apply: faʿīl "Quality' is defined as:
3. build a family of words from a known root and guess the meaning of a new word from root and schema;
4. recognize when the root is weak or double and where to look for it;
5. find a word in a dictionary ordered by root;
6. read a vocalized text of 150 words and collect the words by root.
Two-week plan.

2. The root: an idea, not a word
Almost all Arabic words of Arab origin can be divided into two parts that interweave:
• root ( ⁧جِذْر⁩ ǧiḏr): Usually three consonants, sometimes four, that bring a general idea. No yes It says by itself and writes with separate letters: ⁧ك ت ب⁩ ;

• the scheme ( ⁧وَزْن⁩ wazn, literally weight, measure inserts into the root and decides the category and a part of the meaning. Word = root + scheme. In ⁧كَاتِب⁩ the root is ⁧ك ت ب⁩ , the schema is consonant + ā + consonant + i + consonant

Because you need it. In front of a new word in a title, the root immediately gives you the field of meaning; the scheme tells you if it is a person, a place, an action or a quality. Many times enough to understand; when it's not enough, the root is the address you search for in the dictionary (section 6). The foreign words ( ⁧بَرْلَمَان⁩ , ⁧بَنْك⁩ , ⁧فِيلْم⁩ ) and some very ancient words ( ⁧أَب⁩ , ⁧أُمّ⁩ ) do not have a recognizable pattern: they are learned as blocks. Roots of four consonants. You already know two of them: ⁧ت ر ج م⁩ in ⁧مُتَرْجِم⁩ and ⁧ه ن د س⁩ in ⁧مُهَنْدِس⁩ . They are few and follow their own patterns.
3. The diagram and the letters ⁧ف ع ل⁩

To indicate a pattern without tying it to a root, Arab grammars use the root ⁧ف ع ل⁩ Do not do this: ⁧ف⁩ stands for the first root consonant, ⁧ع⁩ for the second, ⁧ل⁩ for the third. Everything else (vowels, prefixes, doubles) belongs to the scheme.

Read the table vertically: the same scheme gives words of the same type with different roots. Read it horizontally: the same root gives different words with different patterns. The boxes with Two practical rules:
1. The pattern is seen in the vocalization. No vowels ⁧مكتب⁩ could be read in several ways; with the scheme in mind read immediately maktab, why forms mafʿal They're very common.

2. The pattern is also recognized with new roots. If you know that ⁧م ط ع م⁩ is a place and you know ⁧ط ع م⁩ • food, feed ( ⁧طَعَام⁩ ), you understand ⁧مَطْعَم⁩ It is a place where you eat it even without dictionary.

5. How to Find the Root
Always proceed in the same order.

1. Remove what is not word: article ( ⁧ال⁩ ), conjunctions and combined prepositions ( ⁧وَ⁩ , ⁧فَ⁩ , ⁧بِـ⁩ , ⁧لِـ⁩ , ⁧كَـ⁩ ), suffix pronouns ( ⁧ـهُ⁩ , ⁧ـهَا⁩ , ⁧ـهُمْ⁩ ...), gender loss and number ( ⁧ـة⁩ , ⁧ـات⁩ , ⁧ـُونَ⁩ , ⁧ـِينَ⁩ , ⁧ـَانِ⁩ ).
2. Remove the prefixes of the scheme: ⁧مَـ⁩ / ⁧مُـ⁩ (places, instruments, parts), ⁧تَـ⁩ / ⁧تِـ⁩ (action names such as ⁧تَقْرِير⁩ ), ⁧اِ⁩ / ⁧اِسْتِـ⁩ /
⁧اِنْـ⁩ (derived forms: ⁧اِجْتِمَاع⁩ , ⁧اِسْتِقْبَال⁩ ), ⁧أَ⁩ (plurality as ⁧أَقْلَام⁩ ), ⁧يَـ⁩ / ⁧تَـ⁩ / ⁧نَـ⁩ / ⁧أَ⁩ of the imperfect.

3. Remove internal long vowels ( ⁧ا⁩ , ⁧و⁩ , ⁧ي⁩ ) and doubling: almost always they are of the scheme. In ⁧كِتَاب⁩ the ⁧ا⁩ is of schema; in ⁧مُدَرِّس⁩ the ⁧ر⁩ doubled is only worth one ⁧ر⁩ of the root.
4. Three consonants remain: that is the root. If there are two left, go to the section 5.

Warning: the same letters may be of the root or pattern. The ⁧م⁩ is of the in ⁧مَكْتَب⁩ but root in ⁧عَمَل⁩ and in ⁧حُكْم⁩ . The ⁧ت⁩ is of the in ⁧تَقْرِير⁩ but root in ⁧كِتَاب⁩ . Practical rule: try to remove the letter; If what is left does not give a root with a sensible meaning, put it back.
6. Weak roots and double roots (recognize)

Two types of root ... Hide a consonant. You will study them thoroughly in A2-15 and A2-16; For now, you need to know where to look. Weak roots: with ⁧و⁩ or ⁧ي⁩ . ⁧و⁩ and ⁧ي⁩ They are consonant, but in many patterns they become long vowels or disappear.
⁧مُسْتَشْفًى⁩ alif maqṣūra final ⁧ش ف ي⁩ Healing
Double root: second and third matching consonant. They are often written with one letter and one letter. šadda.
Roots with hamza. The hamza is a consonant full of the root, even when it changes support: ⁧سُؤَال⁩ ,
⁧مَسْؤُول⁩ , ⁧يَسْأَلُ⁩ ( ⁧س أ ل⁩ ); ⁧قِرَاءَة⁩ , ⁧يَقْرَأُ⁩ ( ⁧ق ر أ⁩ ).

When two consonants remain. Test in order: one ⁧و⁩ or ⁧ي⁩ in the centre ( ⁧قَالَ⁩ → ⁧ق و ل⁩ ); one ⁧و⁩ or ⁧ي⁩ at the end ( ⁧مُسْتَشْفًى⁩ → ⁧ش ف ي⁩ ); one ⁧و⁩ at the beginning ( ⁧يَصِلُ⁩ → ⁧و ص ل⁩ ); doubling of the second ( ⁧رَدّ⁩ → ⁧ر د د⁩ ).
7. The Dictionary by Root

Many bilingual Arabic dictionaries are sorted by root, not by the first letter of the word: to find ⁧مَعْلُومَات⁩ look for the root ⁧ع ل م⁩ And under that voice, you find the whole family. This is the case of Hans Wehr's Arabic-English dictionary, the most common reference (Appendix C): under each root the simple verb with the vowel of the imperfect and its action names, then the derived forms indicated with Roman numerals (II, III... X), then the names. How to use:
1. find the root with the section method 5;
2. search for the root in Arabic alphabetical order: first the first consonant, then the second, then the third ( ⁧ك ت ب⁩ comes before ⁧ك ث ر⁩ why ⁧ت⁩ comes before ⁧ث⁩ );
3. inside the voice, look for the scheme: a participle (fāʿil, mafʿūl), a place (mafʿal) or an action name;
4. If you don't find anything, the root is probably weak or double: go back to section 6.
Arabic alphabetical order, to remember for the search: ⁧ا ب ت ث ج ح خ د ذ ر ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ع غ ف ق ك ل م⁩
⁧ن ه و ي⁩ .
Many digital apps and dictionaries also search for the whole word. They are comfortable, but the root dictionary shows you the family and helps you remember: use it at least for important words.
8. Root and meaning: traps
The root gives the field, not translation. Three frequent traps:
1. The meaning has specialized. ⁧جَامِعَة⁩ comes from ⁧ج م ع⁩ • bring together, but it means university; ⁧مَجْلِس⁩ comes from
⁧ج ل س⁩ "Sit down" means "consiglio," "assemble" ( ⁧مَجْلِسُ الأَمْنِ⁩ ). Translate the word, not etymology.

2. One root, two fields. ⁧ع م ل⁩ gives ⁧عَمَل⁩ • work • ⁧عَمَلِيَّة⁩ Operation: ⁧عَمِيل⁩ , which means The Bank's (bank's, company's) and, in the political press, its agent serving a foreign power are highly negative. The context decides.
3. Two roots, similar letters. ⁧عِلْم⁩ Science ( ⁧ع ل م⁩ ) e ⁧أَلَم⁩ Pain ( ⁧أ ل م⁩ ) are similar only to one eye Inexperienced: ⁧ع⁩ and ⁧ء⁩ They're different consonants.

9. Pronunciation

The pattern has a rhythm. The long vowels of the scheme attract the accent and must be kept long: kā -Tib, mak- tūb , ki- tāb Mak-ta-ba. Stretch and shorten with precision: kātib "writer" is the name of the manufacturer. kuttāb "Descriptors" are: kitāb The difference is in duration and doubling. Couples that distinguish patterns. The B script alternates them; Repeat in pairs:
⁧عِلْم⁩ – ⁧عَالِم⁩ ʿālim – ʿilm science
⁧حُكْم⁩ – ⁧حَاكِم⁩ ḥākim – ḥukm Governor
The doubling is heard. In ⁧مُعَلِّم⁩ ( muʿallim) e ⁧سُكَّان⁩ ( sukkān) Keep the double consonant for an extra moment, as in English   . Without doubling change your word or scheme.
